title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from pp. 88-90. E and E' are sets, each carrying a saturation (closure) operator s-W°_E, written s-Ψ° in the neighbouring transcriptions. Σ_E is the complete lattice of saturated subsets of E. The symbol |∘| is a 'meets / is not orthogonal to' relation between subsets, apparently nonempty intersection. The key property used is that a saturated set meets A iff it meets the saturation Ā of A, as an open set meets X iff it meets the closure of X.

The data are two relations α: E → P(E') and β: E' → P(E), extended to images ᾱ, β̄ on subsets. Set α_*(S) = sat(ᾱ(S)) and β_*(S') = sat(β̄(S')). Condition (ii) is the 'transposition' condition S |∘| β_*(S') ⇔ α_*(S) |∘| S'. Condition (iii) is the same for arbitrary subsets.

This page finishes the corollary begun on p.88: sat(ᾱ(A)) = sat(ᾱ(Ā)). One inclusion is trivial. For the other it suffices that, for every saturated A', A' meets ᾱ(A) iff A' meets ᾱ(Ā). The struck-out first attempt reduced this via (iii). The kept argument uses (ii)/(iii): the two sides become β_*(A') |∘| A and β_*(A') |∘| Ā. These are equivalent because β_*(A') is saturated and Ā = sat A. Qed.

Specialising to A = {x}: sat(α(x)) = α_*(sat{x}). Define α'(x) := sat(α(x)) ∈ Σ_{E'}; this is the boxed formula α_*(sat{x}) = α'(x). Conversely, for any α, α_*(S) = Sup^{Σ_{E'}}_{x∈S} α'(x) = α'_*(S). So α' : E → Σ_{E'} and the join-preserving map α_* : Σ_E → Σ_{E'} determine each other.

Hence the conditions of 'Prop 3' depend only on α', β'. Next page: given α, β_* is uniquely determined, since S |∘| β_*(S') iff α_*(S) |∘| S'. β_* is the 'transpose' (conjugate) of α_*, and the remaining question is which α_* admit such a transpose.

In modern terms: relational morphisms between closure spaces, reduced to sup-preserving maps between lattices of closed sets. These are required to be conjugate with respect to a 'meets' polarity, in the sense of Jónsson–Tarski conjugate operators (f(a)∧b ≠ 0 ⇔ a∧g(b) ≠ 0).
errors: No mathematical error in the retained argument. It silently uses that a saturated set meets A iff it meets sat(A); presumably this is an axiom or earlier lemma about |∘| and W. The first attempt is correctly struck out.
The machine transcription's 'β_*(A')|∘|Ā'' for the first member should logically be 'β_*(A')|∘|A'. The second member should be 'β_*(A')|∘|Ā'.

ideas.what: Saturation commutes with images of a 'transposable' relation: sat(ᾱ(A)) = sat(ᾱ(sat A))
ideas.modern_name: continuity of a relation w.r.t. closure operators; closure-preserving relational morphism

ideas.what: Correspondence between maps α': E → Σ_{E'} and join-preserving maps α_*: Σ_E → Σ_{E'} via α_*(S) = Sup α'(x)
ideas.modern_name: free sup-lattice on a closure space / sup-lattice morphisms determined on generators

ideas.what: Uniqueness of a 'transposed' β_* with S |∘| β_*(S') ⇔ α_*(S) |∘| S'
ideas.modern_name: conjugate operators (Jónsson–Tarski) / adjoints relative to a polarity

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine lattice and closure-space verification: closures commute with conjugate relations, and join-preserving maps are determined by their values on point closures. It is mildly interesting as evidence of Grothendieck doing order-theoretic and closure-space foundations in 1986. The content itself is standard (Jónsson–Tarski conjugates, Galois connections).
transcription_corrections: The operator written 'sup_{W°_{E'}}' in this page's transcription appears in the image as 's-W°_{E'}'. It is the same saturation operator transcribed as s-Ψ° on p.88, i.e. saturation rather than 'sup'.
'Ā = sat_W A' is in the image roughly 'Ā = s-W A' (saturation of A).
In 'les deux membres équivalent resp. à', the first expression should read β_*(A')|∘|A, not |∘|Ā'.
Last line: 'la donnant' is likely 'les données' or a similar phrasing ('...ne dépendent que des α', β' associés, données de α'_*=α_*, β'_*=β_*').
